title: General Tso's Chicken (Unbreaded Thighs)
description: Restaurant-quality General Tso's with unbreaded chicken thighs and roasted broccoli — big sauce, clean cook, calorie-conscious without sacrificing flavor.

ingredients.name: dried red chili flakes
ingredients.note: Glenn solo batch — reduce to 0.5 tsp for Cindy

steps.title: Roast the broccoli
steps.text: Preheat APO to 425°F, dry heat (or 20-30% steam for slightly less char). Cut {broccoli} into florets — roughly uniform size so they finish together. Toss with {oil-broccoli} and a pinch of kosher salt. Spread on the APO rack in a single layer. Roast 8-10 minutes until edges are charred and florets have color but still have bite. Pull them slightly underdone — they finish in the sauce. Set aside.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.text: In a small bowl, whisk together {coconut-aminos}, {hoisin}, {rice-vinegar}, {broth}, {hot-honey}, and {sesame-oil}. In a separate small bowl, mix {cornstarch-slurry} with 2 tbsp cold water until smooth — this is your slurry. Keep them separate until you're ready to thicken. Pre-mixing the slurry into the sauce causes it to clump when it hits heat.

steps.title: Prep and coat the chicken
steps.text: Cut {thighs} into small pieces — keep them roughly uniform so they cook evenly. Toss with {cornstarch-chicken} and a pinch of kosher salt until lightly coated. This thin coating is not breading — it helps the chicken pick up color and contributes a small amount of body to the sauce.

steps.title: Bloom the aromatics
steps.text: Heat {oil-chicken} in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add {chili-flakes} and cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add {garlic} and {ginger}, stir constantly for another 30 seconds. The goal is fragrant, not brown — burned garlic will make the whole sauce bitter.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Add the coated chicken pieces to the pan in a single layer — don't crowd or they'll steam instead of sear. Cook undisturbed for 2-3 minutes until golden on the bottom, then stir and cook another 2-3 minutes. The chicken doesn't need to be fully cooked through — it finishes in the sauce. Remove to a plate and set aside.

steps.title: Build and thicken the sauce
steps.text: Pour the sauce mixture into the same pan over medium heat. Stir and scrape up any browned bits — that's flavor. Once simmering, give the cornstarch slurry a quick re-stir and stream it in while stirring. The sauce will tighten up within about 60 seconds. Target consistency: thick enough to coat the back of a spoon and cling to the chicken.

steps.title: Finish chicken and broccoli in the sauce
steps.text: Return the seared chicken to the pan along with the roasted broccoli florets. Toss everything to coat thoroughly. Simmer together for 2-3 minutes so the chicken finishes cooking, the broccoli heats through, and both absorb the sauce. Taste and adjust — a touch more rice vinegar brightens it, a touch more hot honey deepens the sweetness.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Plate over Tiger rice cooker rice cooked with Better Than Bouillon and a pat of butter. Garnish with {sesame-seeds}. Sauce should be glossy, clingy, and coating every piece.

notes:
Broccoli: Buy fresh crowns — frozen releases too much water and kills the caramelization. Two crowns yields roughly 12 oz of florets after trimming. Pull them slightly underdone from the APO — they finish in the sauce.

Ginger: 0.5 tsp is intentionally conservative — background warmth only. Taste the sauce before it goes in and add more if you want it.

Chili flakes: 1 tbsp is the Glenn solo batch level. Cut to 0.5 tsp or less when Cindy is eating.

Water chestnuts: Great addition for a Glenn-only batch — stir in when chicken and broccoli return to the pan. Omit for Cindy.

Reheat: Add a splash of broth to loosen the sauce. Freezer-friendly after fully cooked and cooled.

Dual protein: When Cindy is home, run chicken breasts through the same cornstarch coat and sear separately. Combine in the sauce at the end, or keep sauced separately for different heat levels.
